structured_output.analysis: iso_3.15 sits exactly on the budget (84617/26880), and it came from a knapsack over single-layer KL. Single-layer swaps therefore offer little: the retrieved int3-to-int2 downgrades are expensive (model.layers.3.mlp.up_proj goes from 0.0064177 to 0.0302218), and the tabled moves have small positive predicted deltas. The measured KL (0.4361) is also above the additive prediction (0.3983), so interactions or calibration-to-validation generalization may matter. No non-default options have been measured yet, so the option axes are the main unexplored lever, and three of the four grids test them. weight_algo.* options should not change stored bits, assuming the budget counts only weight bits. Their effects are untested hypotheses, with no measured or predicted KL. The fourth grid tests group size as a way to fund upgrades. Bits per weight implied by the table deltas fit n + (16 + n)/group_size: 3.1484 for int3 and 2.1406 for int2 at group_size=128. Assuming that holds at 256, rht_gptq_int3 at group_size=256 saves about 0.0742 bits/weight. The per-layer method map is not in the evidence, so I bounded the saving using the 109 rht_gptq_int3 layers and inferred layer sizes (not in the records) of about 1.05M, 2.10M and 3.15M weights. That gives at least about 12.6M bits saved, against about 12.2M bits for the four upgrades, so the grid should fit but could be refused if these assumptions are wrong. Its risk is added loss across all rht_gptq_int3 layers, which could outweigh the upgrades, and the table's KL values for those methods were measured at default options, so they may not carry over at group_size=256.

proposals.name: iso_actorder_all
proposals.rationale: Tests weight_algo.act_order=true on every GPTQ-family method with no method changes. The effect is unmeasured. Base recipe iso_3.15 measured KL 0.43614466651129274 [E514ab09c524e]. Activation outliers are uneven across channels at model.layers.27.mlp.up_proj, with channel_absmax_ratio 65.2425 [E3c29dce14bae], so the order in which columns are quantized may matter.

proposals.name: iso_damp_high
proposals.rationale: Tests weight_algo.damp=0.05 on every GPTQ-family method with no method changes. The effect is unmeasured. Activations at model.layers.27.mlp.up_proj are heavy-tailed, with kurtosis 1090.09 [E24beed188b6a] and absmax 520.657 [E17ce1bbeaa4a]. Stronger damping may reduce overfitting of the Hessian to calibration outliers and lower validation KL from 0.43614466651129274 [E514ab09c524e].

proposals.name: iso_damp_low
proposals.rationale: Tests weight_algo.damp=0.002 as the opposite direction to the higher-damping grid, with no method changes. The effect is unmeasured. Lighter damping keeps more of the measured Hessian in the error compensation, and the result will be compared with base KL 0.43614466651129274 [E514ab09c524e].

proposals.name: iso_rht3_g256_upgrades
proposals.rationale: Tests whether weight.group_size=256 on rht_gptq_int3 can pay for upgrades to layers where loss concentrates. The whole-recipe effect is unmeasured. At default options, model.layers.14.mlp.down_proj measured 0.00633466 with rht_gptq_int2 [E4c3f9b73e065] and 0.00181478 with rht_gptq_int3 [E90bd4b2f3645]. model.layers.3.mlp.up_proj measured 0.0064177 with rht_gptq_int3 [E6f4f7ea296d5] and 0.00237732 with gptq_int4 [Ef4ee8cb4969e]. Layers model.layers.18.mlp.gate_proj [Eb1dd74cd6447] and model.layers.11.mlp.gate_proj [E9c454f30c659] currently use rht_gptq_int2 and are among the largest losses. Base KL is 0.43614466651129274 [E514ab09c524e].
